_comment: Scoped decision policy for AFK (unattended) delegation. The autonomous decider classifies each grey-area checkpoint against this policy. Only classes in auto_decidable may be resolved without a human; everything in escalate_to_human (and anything unmatched) must go to a human decider (e.g. a Remote Control session). Every decision - auto OR escalated - is written to the audit log. This is an example; copy it to your policy_path and tune.

auto_decidable.when: Two or more approaches are functionally equivalent and reversible (e.g. loop vs formula, equivalent library helpers), with no security, cost, data-loss, or public-API impact.
auto_decidable.bound: Pick the simpler/more-conventional option. If any option changes an interface, a dependency, or a persisted format, do NOT auto-decide.

auto_decidable.when: The spec is silent on a low-stakes default (a log level, an internal file name, ordering of independent steps) and any reasonable choice is acceptable.
auto_decidable.bound: Pick the least-surprising default and record the assumption. Never auto-decide a default that is hard to change later.

escalate_to_human.when: The decision touches auth, permissions, secrets, sandboxing, or trust boundaries.
The decision deletes data, rewrites history, or is otherwise hard to undo.
The decision materially changes cost, scope, a public API, or a persisted data format.
The right answer depends on product intent the executor cannot infer.
